title: SALT
subtitle: The Empire's Smallest Fear
logline: In 1930, the British Raj taxed the one thing every Indian could gather for free. One man picked up a handful of salt, and the Empire discovered a weapon it could not arrest.

style.look: dawn salt flat, deep teal shadows, warm rim light, visible dust, restrained typography
rules: Show the object before the explanation.
One idea per shot. No wall of text.
The camera moves with purpose: push, reveal, or follow. Never drift without a reason.
Sound carries the scale: wind, footsteps, distant surf, a low drone, then silence before the turn.
Violence is implied through sound and aftermath, never lingered on.

blender.role: 3D sets, hero stills, camera moves, render passes, procedural salt flat, marchers, crystals

cascadeur.version: Indie (paid) or Free for non-commercial tests
cascadeur.role: character animation and physics-assisted poses; exported as FBX/GLB
cascadeur.constraint: FBX export requires Indie or Pro. Free exports .casc only. Run on the owner machine, not GitHub Actions.

embergen.role: fire, smoke, dust and fluid simulations; exported as VDB or flipbook
embergen.constraint: Needs a GPU. Bake once on the owner machine and store the VDB/flipbook in assets/vfx/.

blenderkit.role: CC0 and royalty-free props, anatomy, tools and environments
blenderkit.constraint: Record the license and source URL in assets/library/manifest.json.

sketchfab.role: CC0/CC-BY models for monuments, objects and anatomy
sketchfab.constraint: Download only assets whose license allows commercial use. Record attribution.

after_effects.role: online edit, parallax, grade, typography, sound design
after_effects.constraint: Adobe does not run on GitHub Actions. The repository exports layered plates, an EDL and a shot manifest.

premiere_pro.role: final conform, mix and YouTube master
premiere_pro.constraint: Owner-machine finishing step. The CI cut is an animatic, not the final online.

python.role: Blender scene assembly, naming, pass rendering, validation and batch exports

node.role: orchestration, schema validation, ffmpeg assembly, caption and thumbnail generation

scenes.title: A grain
scenes.purpose: Hook with the smallest object in the story.

narration.text: The British Empire could tax almost anything. It chose the one thing the poorest Indian could gather for free.

shots.visual: A single translucent salt crystal on black volcanic stone. One hard rim light. The crystal is almost a jewel, then the light reveals the coarse, ordinary edges.
sfx: a single dry tap as the crystal settles

scenes.title: The tax
scenes.purpose: Make the salt tax concrete, not abstract.

narration.text: The Salt Act of 1882 gave the Raj a monopoly on collection and manufacture. Salt was free on the coast. The law made it a crime to take it.
The tax was small at the till and enormous in a poor family's kitchen. By 1930 it was 8.2 percent of British India's tax revenue.

shots.camera: overhead, locked, slow reveal by a moving light
shots.visual: A colonial ledger, a brass scale, and a cone of coarse salt. The numbers are stamped, not written. A hand in a white sleeve enters and takes a pinch.
shots.transition: match cut on the falling salt

shots.visual: A clay bowl, flatbread, and a small dish of salt in a dim kitchen. The bowl is almost empty. The salt dish is the brightest object in the frame.

scenes.title: The choice
scenes.purpose: Turn a policy story into a duel of judgment.

narration.text: On 2 March 1930, Gandhi wrote to the Viceroy with eleven demands. Abolish the salt tax. Cut military spending. Protect Indian cloth.
Lord Irwin was not impressed. He wrote to London that a salt campaign did not keep him awake at night.

shots.visual: The letter on a dark wooden desk. Ink, a fountain pen, a small spinning wheel in the background. The eleven demands sit under a shaft of light.
A vast Viceroy's office. A tiny figure at a huge desk, framed by columns. The letter is a white speck on the desk.
shots.text: “DOES NOT KEEP ME AWAKE AT NIGHT”

scenes.title: The march
scenes.purpose: The spectacle: small figures, huge land, growing line.

narration.text: On 12 March 1930, Gandhi left Sabarmati with 78 volunteers. They walked for 24 days, 387 kilometres, through 48 villages.
The line grew. Farmers, weavers, students, women. The world's press came to watch a man walk toward the sea.

shots.camera: low wide, 28mm, slow dolly in; silhouettes against a huge dawn sun
shots.visual: A column of marchers crosses a white salt flat. The first figures are close and dark; the line recedes to a thin thread. Heat shimmer, dust, a distant blue sea.
Bare feet, dust, a wooden staff. The rhythm is steady. We never see the face; the crowd is the character.
A dark relief map of western India. A thin gold line runs from Sabarmati to Dandi. Villages light up as the line passes. The sea is a deep teal.

scenes.title: Dandi
scenes.purpose: The turn: a handful of salt becomes a political fact.

narration.text: At 8:30 on the morning of 6 April, Gandhi bent down and picked up a lump of salt.
The law was broken. Within weeks, millions joined. Over 60,000 were jailed.

shots.camera: macro, 85mm, shallow focus, one slow tilt
shots.visual: A weathered hand lifts a wet lump of salt from the mud. The salt glistens. The hand is calm. The background is a white blur of sea and sky.

shots.camera: top-down, fast lateral move across newspapers
shots.visual: Newspaper front pages in different languages. One headline: SALT LAW BROKEN. The camera moves faster as the headlines multiply.

scenes.title: Dharasana
scenes.purpose: Show the cost without exploiting suffering.

narration.text: The Raj answered with lathis. At Dharasana, volunteers walked into the clubs and did not raise a hand.
The world saw the choice the Empire made. The story reached 1,350 newspapers.

shots.camera: wide, locked, then a slow push
shots.visual: A line of unarmed volunteers in white faces a line of police in khaki. The space between them is empty and bright. Dust. A dropped cap. No gore.

narration.text: In March 1931, Gandhi and Irwin signed a pact. Over 90,000 political prisoners were released.
The Raj did not abolish the salt tax. The movement did not win everything. It won something harder to take away: a nation had seen its own power.

shots.visual: A prison gate opens. Light spills out. A crowd waits in silence. The gate is huge; the people are small.

scenes.title: The after
scenes.purpose: Land the idea and the title.

narration.text: The Empire had armies. It had no answer to a man picking up salt.

shots.visual: The salt crystal from the opening returns, now on a black field. It turns slowly. The title SALT resolves beside it. Subtitle: The Empire's Smallest Fear.
